officialTitle: Pembrolizumab versus chemotherapy for previously untreated, PD-L1-expressing, locally advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (KEYNOTE-042): a randomised, open-label, controlled, phase 3 trial

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: From Dec 19, 2014, to March 6, 2017, 1274 patients (902 men, 372 women, median age 63 years [IQR 57-69]) with a PD-L1 TPS of 1% or greater were allocated to pembrolizumab (n=637) or chemotherapy (n=637)

clinicalQuestion: Does first-line pembrolizumab monotherapy improve overall survival over platinum chemotherapy in advanced NSCLC with PD-L1 TPS ≥1%?

pico.population: Previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC, PD-L1 TPS ≥1%, no sensitising EGFR mutation or ALK translocation, ECOG PS 0–1
pico.comparator: Investigator's choice of platinum-based chemotherapy, four to six cycles
pico.outcomes: Primary: OS in TPS ≥50%, ≥20% and ≥1% populations (hierarchical). Safety

arms.label: Pembrolizumab
arms.dosing: 200 mg every 3 weeks for up to 35 cycles
arms.doseSourceQuote: to receive pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks for up to 35 cycles

arms.label: Platinum-based chemotherapy
arms.regimen: Investigator's choice of platinum-based chemotherapy for four to six cycles

publications.title: Pembrolizumab versus chemotherapy for previously untreated, PD-L1-expressing, locally advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (KEYNOTE-042): a randomised, open-label, controlled, phase 3 trial.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: Overall survival was significantly longer in the pembrolizumab group than in the chemotherapy group in all three TPS populations (≥50% hazard ratio 0·69, 95% CI 0·56-0·85, p=0·0003; ≥20% 0·77, 0·64-0·92, p=0·0020, and ≥1% 0·81, 0·71-0·93, p=0·0018). The median surival values by TPS population were 20·0 months (95% CI 15·4-24·9) for pembrolizumab versus 12·2 months (10·4-14·2) for chemotherapy, 17·7 months (15·3-22·1) versus 13·0 months (11·6-15·3), and 16·7 months (13·9-19·7) versus 12·1 months (11·3-13·3), respectively.

safety.description: Treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse
safety.sourceQuote: Treatment-related adverse events of grade 3 or worse occurred in 113 (18%) of 636 treated patients in the pembrolizumab group and in 252 (41%) of 615 in the chemotherapy group and led to death in 13 (2%) and 14 (2%) patients, respectively.

strengths: Large randomised phase III with hierarchical OS testing across PD-L1 strata
limitations: The TPS ≥1% population includes the TPS ≥50% subgroup; the TPS 1–49% stratum was not a separate step in the primary testing hierarchy

clinicalImplications.text: Extended pembrolizumab monotherapy as a first-line option to PD-L1 TPS ≥1% NSCLC without EGFR/ALK alterations, with the clearest benefit in TPS ≥50%.

tumourBoardPearl.text: For TPS 1–49%, the monotherapy signal is weaker; chemo-immunotherapy is generally preferred when the patient can tolerate it.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 30955977 (including the abstract's spelling 'surival').
